proof_nl: Write E_k := k(d-dk-2r)/2 and F := r(1-n)/2. First, E_k is an integer because E_k = d k(1-k)/2 - kr and k(1-k) is always even. Also F is an integer because n ≡ 1 (mod 2d) implies n = 1 + 2dt for some integer t, hence F = -rdt. For any positive integer M, [M]_q = (1-q^M)/(1-q) = 1 + q + ... + q^(M-1), so [3dk+r]_q and [rn]_q lie in Z[q] (here 3dk+r > 0 and rn > 0). Moreover, for each k >= 0, (q^r,q^r,q^d; q^(2d))_k = product_{j=0}^{k-1} (1-q^(r+2dj))^2 (1-q^(d+2dj)) belongs to Z[q], and (q^d; q^d)_k = product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj)) belongs to Z[q]. Also U_{d,n}(q) = product_{j=1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj)) belongs to Z[q]. Now expand G_{d,r,n}(q) = U_{d,n}(q)(T_{d,r,n}(q)-R_{d,r,n}(q)) = U_{d,n}(q)T_{d,r,n}(q) - U_{d,n}(q)R_{d,r,n}(q) in Q(q). For the k-th summand of U_{d,n}(q)T_{d,r,n}(q), use (q^(2d); q^(2d))_k = product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(2dj)) = product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj))(1+q^(dj)). Then U_{d,n}(q) * (q^d; q^d)_k^2 / (q^(2d); q^(2d))_k = [product_{j=1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj))] [product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj))^2] / [product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj))(1+q^(dj))] = [product_{j=1}^k (1-q^(dj))] [product_{j=k+1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj))] = (q^d; q^d)_k product_{j=k+1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj)), where the product is 1 if k = n-1. Therefore G_{d,r,n}(q) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d; q^(2d))_k (q^d; q^d)_k q^(E_k) product_{j=k+1}^{n-1} (1+q^(dj)) - U_{d,n}(q)[rn]_q q^F, which is exactly the expanded expression stated in the lemma. Finally, each summand in that finite sum lies in Z[q,q^(-1)]: all factors other than q^(E_k) lie in Z[q], while q^(E_k) is a Laurent monomial because E_k is an integer. Likewise U_{d,n}(q)[rn]_q q^F lies in Z[q,q^(-1)]. Since Z[q,q^(-1)] is closed under finite sums and differences, G_{d,r,n}(q) belongs to Z[q,q^(-1)]. Hence the lemma is proved.
solver_summary: Multiplying T_{d,r,n}(q) by U_{d,n}(q) clears the denominator (q^(2d);q^(2d))_k termwise because 1-q^(2dj) = (1-q^(dj))(1+q^(dj)). This yields the displayed expanded formula, and every resulting term is a polynomial in q times an integral power of q, hence lies in Z[q,q^(-1)]. The same is true for U_{d,n}(q)R_{d,r,n}(q), so their difference G_{d,r,n}(q) is a Laurent polynomial with integer coefficients.
